key.description:
Setting key being updated; must equal the `{key}` path parameter. The number-valued settings:
- `rate_limit.api_key.per_minute` — Global default for tenant-scoped API keys on /v1/* routes (requests per window).
- `rate_limit.api_key.window_ms` — Sliding-window length for the per-key rate limit (milliseconds).
- `rate_limit.mcp_tenant.per_minute` — Tenant-mode MCP (mcp:read) budget. Defaults to parity with regular API keys — tenant-mode agents do legitimate cross-customer analytics.
- `rate_limit.mcp_end_user.per_minute` — End-user MCP (mcp:read on eut_ tokens) budget. Keyed on end_user:<id> so two agent installs for the same customer share the budget. Tighter default — a single customer Q&A agent does not need 600/min.
- `rate_limit.connect_link.per_minute` — Public /connect/{token} flow rate limit, keyed on client IP. Stops brute-force token guessing without throttling legitimate retries.
- `connect_link.default_expiry_hours` — Default expiry for newly minted Connect Links when none is set on the form.
- `data_store.sync.default_interval_minutes` — Minutes between syncs for connections on the default schedule. Each sync re-reads every resource from the platform, so a shorter interval costs platform API calls. Held to 15–43200 (30 days); 0 or less means the built-in 360.
- `webhooks.delivery_retention_days` — Days to keep DELIVERED and DEAD outbound webhook deliveries. Their body column holds the full event JSON — customer emails and connection detail included — so unbounded retention is a data-protection liability, not just disk. Defaults to 30 days (delivery bodies are an operational log); set 0 to keep forever. Pending deliveries are never pruned; swept every ~6h by the delivery worker. Existing deployments keep whatever value they already have (seeding never overwrites).
- `webhooks.inbound_event_retention_days` — Days to keep raw INBOUND platform webhook payloads (inbound_events) — order data and other customer PII arrives in these verbatim. 0 = keep forever (the default). Swept together with delivery retention.
- `audit_log.retention_days` — Days of audit-log history to retain. 0 keeps everything forever. When positive, a daily background sweep deletes entries older than this many days (and records an audit.retention.prune entry when it removes any).
- `logos.fetch_delay_ms` — Milliseconds between Brandfetch requests during a logo fetch. Brandfetch publishes 1,000 requests per 5 minutes per IP. 400ms holds the worst case (every logo found on the first attempt, which costs one request and one delay) at 150/min = 750 per 5 minutes. Lower it only if you have an agreement with Brandfetch.
- `logos.job_retention_days` — Days of finished logo-fetch job history to keep. 0 keeps everything forever. Deleting the stored logos clears the history too, since those rows describe fetches whose output no longer exists; the audit log keeps the record either way.

key.description:
Setting key being updated; must equal the `{key}` path parameter. The boolean-valued settings:
- `features.mcp_enabled` — When false, the integration-server refuses any token carrying mcp:read (403 MCP_DISABLED). Use for emergency disable without redeploying.
- `features.end_user_mode_enabled` — When false, /v1/me/* routes are not mounted, so they 404. Read once at boot — unlike features.mcp_enabled, a change here needs a restart. End-user mode in MCP and the admin mint UX are inert until this is true.
- `features.test_mode_enabled` — When false, the /test/v1/* sandbox refuses every request (503 TEST_MODE_DISABLED) within one settings poll. The live /v1/* surface is untouched either way, and test-mode API keys can still be minted and revoked — they simply have nothing to call.
- `connect_link.one_time_default` — When true, new Connect Links default to one-time read-only mode. Templates and explicit form picks always win.
- `auth.local_login_enabled` — When false, username/password login is rejected for everyone EXCEPT the pinned break-glass admin. Only disable once an SSO provider is verified working.
- `auth.dev_api_keys_enabled` — When false, the integration-server refuses osk_ developer keys on /v1/* with 403 API_KEYS_DISABLED. Read per request, so a flip applies without a redeploy. Refused unless an OIDC issuer is enabled, reachable by somebody, and has actually verified a token — otherwise switching this off locks every developer out. X-Admin-Secret is never gated by it.
- `auth.dev_oauth_enabled` — When true, /v1/* also accepts an OIDC bearer token from an issuer registered under OAuth clients. Defaults off because it means nothing until an issuer exists. Read per request, like features.mcp_enabled.
- `auth.sandbox_self_serve_enabled` — When true, POST /test/v1/keys mints a sandbox API key with NO authentication — a developer evaluating this deployment gets a test key without asking an admin. Each key belongs to a fresh throwaway tenant, works only on the no-egress /test/v1/* sandbox, expires after 7 days, and minting is IP-rate-limited. Bulk-revoke via the mode=test filter on the API keys page. Read per request.
- `data_store.raw_payload.payments` — When true, payments resources carry the full upstream payload under \`raw\`. Off by default: across the payments adapters that payload declares bank account numbers, IBANs and card numbers the canonical schema does not expose (it exposes last4). Card security codes are stripped either way — PCI DSS 3.3.1 permits no exception. Turning this off does NOT clean rows already written, and turning it on does NOT backfill rows already cached — clear the cache after either change.
- `data_store.raw_payload.accounting` — When true, accounting resources carry the full upstream payload under \`metadata\`. Off by default: 17 accounting adapters declare IBAN, bank account or routing numbers there, and the canonical schema has no IBAN field. Turning this off does NOT clean rows already written, and turning it on does NOT backfill rows already cached — clear the cache after either change.
- `data_store.sync.scheduler_enabled` — When false, nothing is synced on a schedule: default and custom schedules wait, and one-time connections without a first sync wait for it. Sync now, the API and the sync right after a Connect Link still run.
- `data_access.mask_financial` — When true, fields classified \`financial\` (amounts, balances, prices) are masked in the admin data viewer and its exports, filters on them are refused, and dashboard metrics that sum them are withheld. Off by default: financial values are tagged but shown to anyone with \`data:read\`. Personal data is masked regardless of this setting unless the reader holds \`data:read_pii\`.

post.summary: First-run admin bootstrap (only succeeds when no users exist)
post.description: Bootstrap the first `admin` account on a fresh deployment and return a JWT for it. Only succeeds while the user table is empty — returns `409` once any user exists. When the server is started with a `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`, the matching token must be supplied in the `X-Bootstrap-Token` header (else `401`), so a fresh or wiped deployment cannot be claimed by an attacker. When NO token is configured, setup is refused from non-loopback addresses (`403`) — a remote first-run must carry a `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`; only a caller on the deployment host may set up tokenless. The created admin is auto-pinned as the break-glass account so SSO can be locked down later without losing password access. Returns `400` if username or password is missing.

get.description: Return the decoded JWT claims (id, username, role) for the currently authenticated operator, plus the caller's effective role (`roleId`, `roleName`), `permissions` and tenant `scope`. The last three are read from the database on each call (cached for a few seconds), so they reflect a role or scope change made since the token was issued. Any authenticated operator may call this; useful for confirming a token is valid and discovering what the caller may do. Returns `401` if the token is missing or invalid.

put.description: Store a profile picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 512 KB) for a console account, replacing any existing one — including one fetched from the identity provider, which SSO then no longer replaces. Any signed-in user may set their own; setting another user’s needs `users:manage`, and is refused (`403`) when that account holds more than you or sees tenants outside your scope. The type is identified from the bytes: `415` for anything else (SVG included, whatever the data URL declares), `413` when too large, `400` when `data` is not base64. `404` for an unknown user. Writes a `user.avatar_update` audit entry.

Any signed-in user may remove their own; removing another user’s needs `users:manage`, with the same `403` escalation guards as uploading. A picture sourced from the identity provider comes back at the next SSO sign-in if the IdP still sends one. `404` for an unknown user. Writes a `user.avatar_delete` audit entry when a picture was removed.

A role cannot become admin-based while any holder is limited to specific tenants (`409`): admins always have every tenant. Requires `roles:manage`. Returns `404` if the role does not exist, `409` for a built-in role (they are immutable) or a taken name, and `403` when either the role as it stands or the edit would grant a permission or base role you do not hold. get.summary: List connections to filter a dashboard by
get.description: The connections in your tenant scope that a dashboard's connection filter can offer, with the adapters among them — narrowed to `vertical`, to a stored dashboard's pinned tenants when `dashboard` is given (your scope ∩ its pins), to one adapter with `platform`, and by `search`, a case-insensitive substring of the connection id or label (an id prefix is enough). `platforms` lists the adapters of the vertical's connections you can see, with counts, ignoring `search` and `platform`. Connections carry only an id, a label, an adapter and a vertical: never a tenant id, a status or a credential, and a connection outside your scope is absent even when searched for by its exact id. `limit` caps the list (default 50, at most 200; other values are clamped); `total` counts every match. Requires `dashboards:view` and `connections:read`. `400` for an unknown vertical or a malformed adapter, `404` for a dashboard you cannot see.

The bootstrap job never changes these. Requires `dashboards:share_all` and access to every tenant (`403 SCOPE_RESTRICTED` for a tenant-restricted caller, since registry entries are deployment-wide). `404` for a dashboard you cannot open, `409 SUPERSET_DISABLED` when Superset is not configured. Writes a `superset.share` audit entry.

post.description: A guest token for one registered dashboard, valid for 5 minutes, carrying a row-level-security clause that limits every query to your tenant scope, narrowed to the dashboard’s pinned tenants when it has any (no clause only when you see every tenant and it is unpinned). Requires `dashboards:view` (and the dashboard’s extra permission, if any). `404` for a dashboard you may not open, `403 SCOPE_EMPTY` when your access is restricted to no tenants, `409 SUPERSET_DISABLED` when Superset is not configured, `502 SUPERSET_UNAVAILABLE` when Superset refuses or cannot be reached. Writes a `superset.guest_token` audit entry at most once per user and dashboard every 10 minutes.

post.description: Create a destination. `config` and `secrets` follow the type's schemas (`GET /api/destinations/types`); secrets are stored encrypted and never returned. `scope` must lie inside your own (`403` `SCOPE_EXCEEDS_CALLER`); `includePii` needs `data:read_pii` (`403` `PII_NOT_PERMITTED`) and records you as approver. Every host named must be public unless allow-listed (`400` `HOST_NOT_ALLOWED`). Requires `destinations:manage`; audited as `destination.create`.

requestBody.description: Request body to create a destination.

get.description: One destination. `404` when unknown or outside your scope. Requires `destinations:manage`.

patch.description: Change a destination’s name, config, scope, PII setting, interval or enabled state. Changing the config, scope or PII of a PII destination needs `data:read_pii`; turning it off or disabling it does not. Widening the scope does not re-export skipped rows: run a backfill. Requires `destinations:manage`; audited as `destination.update`.

requestBody.description: Request body to change a destination.

Values are write-only: the response lists only the names set, and the audit row (`destination.credentials_rotate`) records names only. On a PII destination this needs `data:read_pii`. Requires `destinations:manage`.

post.description: Build the sink with the stored credentials and prove it can write: a probe object in the bucket, or `CREATE` on the Postgres schema. A failed test still answers `200` with `ok: false` and the reason. Requires `destinations:manage`; audited as `destination.test`.

Start an export run now, outside the schedule. `202` with the run id; `409` `RUN_IN_PROGRESS` when one is already running, `409` `DESTINATION_DISABLED` when it is disabled. Requires `destinations:manage`; audited as `destination.run`.

Reset the export cursors — all of them, one vertical’s, or one resource type’s — so the next run re-exports every stored record in scope, then start a run unless `run: false`. Consumers should deduplicate on `_pk`. Requires `destinations:manage`; audited as `destination.backfill`.

post.description: Create or update the roles, schemas and views now (managed mode only; `409` `MANUAL_MODE` otherwise — use the provisioning script). Deployment-wide, so it needs an all-tenant scope (`403` `SCOPE_TOO_NARROW`). `409` `POSTGRES_REQUIRED` on SQLite. Requires `sql_access:manage`; audited as `sql_access.provision`.

get.description: The provisioning SQL as `text/plain` (one `BEGIN … COMMIT` transaction), for manual mode: run it as a role with CREATEROLE. Needs an all-tenant scope. `409` `POSTGRES_REQUIRED` on SQLite. Requires `sql_access:manage`.

get.description: Every view a SQL login can read, with each column’s type in the masked and unmasked schemas and its classification. Requires `data:read`. `409` `POSTGRES_REQUIRED` on SQLite.

post.description: Create a read-only Postgres login. The response carries its password ONCE (`Cache-Control: no-store`); it is never stored or logged — rotate it if lost. The scope must lie inside yours (`403` `SCOPE_EXCEEDS_CALLER`); `pii: true` needs `data:read_pii` (`403` `PII_NOT_ALLOWED`). `409` `NOT_PROVISIONED` before the views exist, `409` `POSTGRES_REQUIRED` on SQLite. Requires `sql_access:manage`; audited as `sql_access.principal_create` (without the password).

post.description: Generate a new password, returned ONCE (`Cache-Control: no-store`). The old one stops working immediately and open sessions are ended. `404` for a principal unknown or outside your scope. Requires `sql_access:manage`; audited as `sql_access.principal_rotate` (without the password).

delete.description: Revoke a login: it can no longer sign in, loses its grants and scope, and its open sessions are ended. The record stays, marked `revoked`. Requires `sql_access:manage`; audited as `sql_access.principal_revoke`.
